cells.tense: You can take a pile of loose thoughts and set them into one line, and you keep a practice where that gets done.
cells.ask: Before you sit down today, spend ten minutes writing the single line you will work on, then take it into the practice and leave it there.
cells.core:
What this looks like when it is going well: a small practice you keep to yourself, no audience and no good week required. Loose ends from the day come in with you, you set them into one line, and you work on that line inside the sitting. Nothing has to be figured out before you begin, because the figuring happens in there.

What keeps it that way is not adding more to it. The hour stays sharp when you leave something out on purpose, and fairness is where that can slip. Give one turn away today without keeping count of what it returns, and tomorrow's hour stays clean.
cells.sheetLine: You gather scattered thoughts into one line, and you keep a practice for it.
cells.verb: gathering scattered thoughts into one working line
cells.place: inside a practice you keep to yourself

cells.tense: You are already arranging the next practice before this one has had its say.
cells.ask: Today, stop the moment the session stops feeling like it is going well, and leave it there without adding one more pass at it.
cells.core:
When this is working, the day's loose thoughts come into your practice and leave as one line you can work on, all inside the sitting. That is what the hour is for, and it does not ask to be planned.

What happens instead is that half your attention has already walked out of the room. Thoughts get gathered into plans for a session that hasn't happened, and the arranging starts standing in for the doing. It feels like holding the thread, and holding the thread is exactly what has gotten loud. The gathering settles only when it stays inside the hour you are in, not the one you are forecasting. What steadies it is letting the session end on a note you did not pick.
cells.sheetLine: You gather the next practice instead of the one in front of you.

cells.tense: You stopped bringing the loose thoughts to your practice a while back, and the practice itself stayed.
cells.ask: Sit ten minutes at the same hour for three days, bring one thought from your day, say one sentence about it out loud, then stop.
cells.core:
In the good version, the day's loose thoughts come into a practice kept to yourself and leave as one line you can work on. The sitting is still there. That much held.

What went quiet is quieter than quitting. The day's loose ends no longer arrive at the practice, and the practice no longer arrives at the day. Two rooms with the door shut between them. It is not that there is nothing left to bring; the walking in stopped. The first thing back is the feel of one thing set down, not the sitting itself. Tomorrow, give ten minutes to one thought you drag in, say one sentence about it out loud, and stop.
cells.sheetLine: The practice stayed. What stopped is you bringing anything to it.

cells.tense: You gather loose thoughts into one line most weeks and call it just how your work goes.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you actually do to keep your practice going, and say plainly that you are the one who does it.
cells.core:
Here is the shape when it is going well: a practice you keep, where the day's loose thoughts come in and leave as one line you can work on. Nobody handed you that, and it runs most weeks.

The part that isn't running is your name on it. You gather the thoughts and hold the hour, and you would say the work does that by itself. People around you lean on the regularity without knowing where it comes from, least of all you. Showing someone the plainest way you keep your own practice is the same act done in front of another person. Explaining why you do it this way and not another isn't dilution. Say out loud that you are the one doing it.

attempts.check: The record only supports gathering thoughts into one working line inside a chosen practice, not that the person actually sits down to practice it; a reader could say they already have a working method, or that their problem is not thought-gathering at all. The ask survives a wrong read if the person can test it in ten minutes and has to say something back on paper either way. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'In practice, scattered thoughts arrive as other people's timing' — it decorates the mechanism, so I cut it.
